verified.source:
# Keep track of what needs doing.
app Todos
Given
 Todo { title:text trim min=1 max=200 label="Task", done:bool=false label={text="Status",values={true="Done",false="Open"}} } label="Todo"
 policy Todo read=members
 fixture task=Todo {title="Try Can"}
When
 crud Todo by=members fields=title,done label={create="Add task"}
  examples update record=task
   as,changes.done,request.record.version -> record.done
   members,true,1 -> true
   members,true,0 -> error(conflict)
   public,true,1 -> error(forbidden)
Then
 preferences { view:enum(all,open,done)=all label={text="Show",values={all="All",open="Open",done="Done"}} }
 page / title="Todos"
  card "Add a task"
   form Todo.create fields=title display=inline
    input title
  card "Your tasks"
   tabs preferences.view
   list Todo as task where preferences.view==all or (preferences.view==open and not task.done) or (preferences.view==done and task.done) order=-created search=title empty="No tasks here. Add a task or choose another view."
    text row.title,row.done
    edit fields=title,done
    tooltip "Permanently delete this task"
     delete
verified.existing: Then owns components, queries, canonical form/action bindings and finite appearance. Shared UI owns daisyUI themes, layout, settings, validation/errors and interactions. There is no current general CSS/prompt-styling syntax. The prior typed css map is only a proposal.
verified.human: User authorizes repairing empty preferences Settings, is exploring prompt-driven frontend styling, rejects verbatim CSS in Can, asks whether saved nondeterministic styling results make sense, and explicitly chose keep exploring rather than selecting prompt-only versus prompt+typed overrides.

state.comparison: Compare these draft architectures for describing component appearance in natural language, with broad visual flexibility and saved nondeterministic outcomes. All candidates retain existing component structure, operation/query bindings, authentication and field authority, generated inputs, errors and focus behavior. No candidate is already implemented. A proposed named style scope would contain ordinary Then components; the AI receives static templates/hooks, declared structure and pinned theme assets, not business records. Generated output is scoped CSS; Can continues to define composition and behavior.

architecture.instructions: Choose the best architecture for exploratory prompt styling when repeatable builds, controlled regeneration, source-owned intent, reviewable appearance and practical implementation simplicity are evaluated together.

criteria.saved_generation: Use a named Then style scope and explicit AI generation during authoring/build preparation. Persist CSS plus a small scope/input-digest/generator/artifact record; reuse it on ordinary builds, diagnose missing/stale output, preview candidates and accept diffs deliberately. It needs a language scope and artifact lifecycle.
criteria.request_generation: Generate CSS from the prompt on browser requests and save the first result for reuse. This can provide an immediate first view; it must control concurrent writers, variable latency/cost, model changes and artifact admission while users are accessing the app.
criteria.design_tool: Keep AI styling an optional design tool producing committed CSS from annotations or external prompts against selected static components. Ordinary builds consume its assets. Language mechanics stay simpler, while prompt/scope ownership and currentness need tool conventions rather than a first-class Then construct.
criteria.open: Leave architecture open if none presently satisfies the shared outcomes; no implementation decision is required.
